ref: 2.15 (ANF Book II ch. XV "Of the Fourth Day"; BKV division 32)
greek: Ὡσαύτως καὶ αἱ τρεῖς ἡμέραι πρὸ τῶν φωστήρων γεγονυῖαι τύποι εἰσὶν τῆς τριάδος, τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοῦ λόγου αὐτοῦ καὶ τῆς σοφίας αὐτοῦ.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 32, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: In like manner also the three days which were before the luminaries, are types of the Trinity, of God, and His Word, and His wisdom.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: The three days before the luminaries are types of the Triad: God, His Word and His Wisdom.
limits: Only use of trias in the extant work (full BKV Greek search, divisions 1-86). The list is typological (days as types), not a doctrine of three persons; the Spirit is not named here. Dods renders triados as "Trinity", a translator's choice.

greek: τετάρτῳ δὲ τόπῳ ἐστὶν ἄνθρωπος ὁ προσδεὴς τοῦ φωτός, ἵνα ᾖ θεός, λόγος, σοφία, ἄνθρωπος. διὰ τοῦτο καὶ τετάρτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγενήθησαν φωστῆρες.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 32, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: And the fourth is the type of man, who needs light, that so there may be God, the Word, wisdom, man. Wherefore also on the fourth day the lights were made.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: The fourth item is the type of man, so that there may be God, the Word, Wisdom, man.
limits: Word and Wisdom are listed as separate items beside God in a numerical schema; no term for person or hypostasis. It does not say the Word and Wisdom are uncreated.

greek: ταῦτα δὲ δεῖγμα καὶ τύπον ἐπέχει μεγάλου μυστηρίου. ὁ γὰρ ἥλιος ἐν τύπῳ θεοῦ ἐστιν, ἡ δὲ σελήνη ἀνθρώπου. καὶ ὥσπερ ὁ ἥλιος πολὺ διαφέρει τῆς σελήνης δυνάμει καὶ δόξῃ, οὕτως πολὺ διαφέρει ὁ θεὸς τῆς ἀνθρωπότητος καὶ καθάπερ ὁ ἥλιος πλήρης πάντοτε διαμένει μὴ ἐλάσσων γινόμενος, οὕτως πάντοτε ὁ θεὸς τέλειος διαμένει, πλήρης ὢν πάσης δυνάμεως καὶ συνέσεως καὶ σοφίας καὶ ἀθανασίας καὶ πάντων τῶν ἀγαθῶν·
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 32, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: And these contain the pattern and type of a great mystery. For the sun is a type of God, and the moon of man. And as the sun far surpasses the moon in power and glory, so far does God surpass man. And as the sun remains ever full, never becoming less, so does God always abide perfect, being full of all power, and understanding, and wisdom, and immortality, and all good.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: The lights contain the pattern and type of a great mystery; the sun is a type of God and the moon of man, and God always abides perfect.
limits: Shows the frame of typology in which "types of the Triad" occurs; it does not name the mystery as the Trinity. Sun-and-moon analogy is about God and man, not the Word.

greek: ἡ δὲ σελήνη κατὰ μῆνα φθίνει καὶ δυνάμει ἀποθνήσκει, ἐν τύπῳ οὖσα ἀνθρώπου, ἔπειτα ἀναγεννᾶται καὶ αὔξει εἰς δεῖγμα τῆς μελλούσης ἔσεσθαι ἀναστάσεως.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 32, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: But the moon wanes monthly, and in a manner dies, being a type of man; then it is born again, and is crescent, for a pattern of the future resurrection.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: The waning and renewed moon is a type of man and a pattern of the future resurrection.
limits: Neutral context for the typology; no Trinitarian content by itself. Listed because the same typology is used for the Triad.

ref: 2.13 (ANF Book II ch. XIII "Remarks on the Creation of the World"; BKV division 30)
greek: πνεῦμα δὲ τὸ ἐπιφερόμενον ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος ὃ ἔδωκεν ὁ θεὸς εἰς ζωογόνησιν τῇ κτίσει, καθάπερ ἀνθρώπῳ ψυχήν, τῷ λεπτῷ τὸ λεπτὸν συγκεράσας (τὸ γὰρ πνεῦμα λεπτὸν καὶ τὸ ὕδωρ λεπτόν), ὅπως τὸ μὲν πνεῦμα τρέφῃ τὸ ὕδωρ, τὸ δὲ ὕδωρ σὺν τῷ πνεύματι τρέφῃ τὴν κτίσιν διϊκνούμενον πανταχόσε.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 30, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: And by the Spirit which is borne above the waters, he means that which God gave for animating the creation, as he gave life to man, mixing what is fine with what is fine. For the Spirit is fine, and the water is fine, that the Spirit may nourish the water, and the water penetrating everywhere along with the Spirit, may nourish creation.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: The Spirit borne above the waters is what God gave to animate creation, as He gave life to man.
limits: Here the Spirit is a gift for animating creation, not a divine person acting; English and Greek agree. This is the passage a reader would use to claim the Spirit is not a distinct person.

greek: ἓν μὲν τὸ πνεῦμα φωτὸς τόπον ἐπέχον ἐμεσίτευεν τοῦ ὕδατος καὶ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, ἵνα τρόπῳ τινὶ μὴ κοινωνῇ τὸ σκότος τῷ οὐρανῷ ἐγγυτέρῳ ὄντι τοῦ θεοῦ, πρὸ τοῦ εἰπεῖν τὸν θεόν·
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 30, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: For the Spirit being one, and holding the place of light, was between the water and the heaven, in order that the darkness might not in any way communicate with the heaven, which was nearer God, before God said, Let there be light.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: The Spirit, being one, holds the place of light between the water and the heaven.
limits: The word "one" is the only unity hint; the sentence is cosmology and does not identify the Spirit with God or with Wisdom.

greek: Ἡ διάταξις οὖν τοῦ θεοῦ, τοῦτό ἐστιν ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ, φαίνων ὥσπερ λύχνος ἐν οἰκήματι συνεχομένῳ, ἐφώτισεν τὴν ὑπ’ οὐρανόν, χωρὶς μὲν τοῦ κόσμου ποιήσας.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 30, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: The command, then, of God, that is, His Word, shining as a lamp in an enclosed chamber, lit up all that was under heaven, when He had made light apart from the world.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: The command of God, that is His Word, shining as a lamp, lit up all that was under heaven when He had made light apart from the world.
limits: Theophilus equates the Word with God's command (diatagē) and with a lamp; a functional reading of the Word can rest on this wording. Compare 2.10 where the Word is begotten (outside this assignment).

greek: ἔτι οὖν συνέχοντος τοῦ ὕδατος τὴν γῆν, μάλιστα κοίλους τόπους, ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ λόγου αὐτοῦ τὸ ὕδωρ συναχθῆναι εἰς συναγωγὴν μίαν, καὶ ὁρατὴν γενηθῆναι τὴν ξηράν, πρότερον γεγονυῖαν αὐτὴν ἀόρατον.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 30, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: The water, then, covering all the earth, and specially its hollow places, God, through His Word, next caused the waters to be collected into one collection, and the dry land to become visible, which formerly had been invisible.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: God, through His Word, caused the waters to be gathered into one place.
limits: Instrumental agency ("through the Word"); a reader hostile to the Word's divinity would take it as a tool. Not checked against any scholarly source in this run.

ref: 2.18 (ANF Book II ch. XVIII "The Creation of Man"; BKV division 35)
greek: ἔτι μὴν καὶ ὡς βοηθείας χρῄζων ὁ θεὸς εὑρίσκεται λέγων· “Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ’ εἰκόνα καὶ καθ’ ὁμοίωσιν.” οὐκ ἄλλῳ δέ τινι εἴρηκεν· “Ποιήσωμεν”, ἀλλ’ ἢ τῷ ἑαυτοῦ λόγῳ καὶ τῇ ἑαυτοῦ σοφίᾳ.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 35, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: Moreover, God is found, as if needing help, to say, Let Us make man in Our image, after Our likeness. But to no one else than to His own Word and wisdom did He say, Let Us make.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: God said "Let Us make" to no one else than His own Word and His Wisdom.
limits: Plural address to Word and Wisdom only; the Spirit is not named in the passage. "His own" is the usual defence point against creaturehood, not checked against scholarship here.

greek: πάντα γὰρ λόγῳ ποιήσας ὁ θεὸς καὶ τὰ πάντα πάρεργα ἡγησάμενος μόνον ἰδίων ἔργον χειρῶν ἄξιον ἡγεῖται τὴν ποίησιν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 35, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: For God having made all things by His Word, and having reckoned them all mere bye-works, reckons the creation of man to be the only work worthy of His own hands.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: God made all things by His Word and treats the making of man as the one work worthy of His own hands.
limits: Creation "by the Word" is instrumental language; it has to be read with 2.10, where the Word is begotten before all things (2.10 is outside this assignment).

ref: 2.16 (ANF Book II ch. XVI "Of the Fifth Day"; BKV division 33)
greek: Τῇ δὲ πέμπτῃ ἡμέρᾳ τὰ ἐκ τῶν ὑδάτων ἐγενήθη ζῶα, δι’ ὧν καὶ ἐν τούτοις δείκνυται . τίς γὰρ δύναιτ’ ἂν τὴν ἐν αὐτοῖς πληθὺν καὶ γονὴν παμποίκιλον ἐξαριθμῆσαι;
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 33, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: On the fifth day the living creatures which proceed from the waters were produced, through which also is revealed the manifold wisdom of God in these things; for who could count their multitude and very various kinds?
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: On the fifth day creatures from the waters were made, "through which also" the manifold wisdom of God is shown (English only).
limits: The BKV Greek has a blank exactly where ANF has "the manifold wisdom of God" (after "δείκνυται"). The Greek for Wisdom in 2.16 is NOT verified; do not quote the gap as Greek. Needs Otto or Grant.

ref: 2.17 (ANF Book II ch. XVII "Of the Sixth Day"; BKV division 34)
greek: Ἕκτῃ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ θεὸς ποιήσας τὰ τετράποδα καὶ τὰ θηρία καὶ ἑρπετὰ τὰ χερσαῖα τὴν πρὸς αὐτὰ εὐλογίαν παρασιωπᾷ, τηρῶν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ τὴν εὐλογίαν, ὃν ἤμελλεν ἐν τῇ ἕκτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ποιεῖν.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 34, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: And on the sixth day, God having made the quadrupeds, and wild beasts, and the land reptiles, pronounced no blessing upon them, reserving His blessing for man, whom He was about to create on the sixth day.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: On the sixth day God made the quadrupeds and wild beasts and pronounced no blessing on them, reserving it for man.
limits: Negative result: no Word, Wisdom, Spirit or Trinity term in the 2.17 Greek (accent-insensitive check on BKV text). Neutral; shows that 2.16-17 carry no Trinitarian content.

ref: 2.14 (ANF Book II ch. XIV "The World Compared to the Sea"; BKV division 31)
greek: Τὸν δὲ κόσμον ἐν ὁμοιώματι ἡμῖν λέγομεν εἶναι τῆς θαλάσσης. ὥσπερ γὰρ θάλασσα, εἰ μὴ εἶχεν τὴν τῶν ποταμῶν καὶ πηγῶν ἐπίρρυσιν καὶ ἐπιχορηγίαν εἰς τροφήν, διὰ τὴν ἁλμυρότητα αὐτῆς πάλαι ἂν ἐκπεφρυγμένη ἦν, οὕτως καὶ ὁ κόσμος, εἰ μὴ ἐσχήκει τὸν τοῦ θεοῦ νόμον καὶ τοὺς προφήτας ῥέοντας καὶ πηγάζοντας τὴν γλυκύτητα καὶ εὐσπλαγχνίαν καὶ δικαιοσύνην καὶ διδαχὴν τῶν ἁγίων ἐντολῶν τοῦ θεοῦ, διὰ τὴν κακίαν καὶ ἁμαρτίαν τὴν πληθύουσαν ἐν αὐτῷ ἤδη ἂν ἐκλελοίπει.
greek_edition: Greek as displayed on the BKV (Bibliothek der Kirchenväter) comparison page, division id 31, read by curl. The page names no print edition in the text read (footnote: 'Following Wolf's reading'). Not checked against Otto 1861 (archive.org copy blocked). Whitespace normalised, letters unaltered.
english: And we say that the world resembles the sea. For as the sea, if it had not had the influx and supply of the rivers and fountains to nourish it, would long since have been parched by reason of its saltness; so also the world, if it had not had the law of God and the prophets flowing and welling up sweetness, and compassion, and righteousness, and the doctrine of the holy commandments of God, would long before now have come to ruin, by reason of the wickedness and sin which abound in it.
translator: Marcus Dods (ANF vol. 2, as on newadvent.org)
edition: English: Ante-Nicene Fathers vol. 2 (Buffalo 1885), as printed on newadvent.org. Greek: BKV web text, no print edition named.
what_it_says: The world is compared to the sea, which would dry up without the rivers; the law and prophets are its fresh water and holy churches are its harbours.
limits: Church imagery only; "holy churches" (ἐκκλησίας ἁγίας) is the only Church term in 2.14. No Trinitarian content.
